subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should canonical literal `openai` session route state be owned for doctor cleanup by the OpenAI provider contract, the Codex doctor contract, or a generic provider-state repair path?
rationale: Literal `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider id and the route used when OpenAI models run through Codex-backed auth/runtime paths, so automation should not choose the permanent ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an `extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts` owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and focused auto-fallback cleanup tests, leaving Codex to legacy aliases and Codex runtime ids.

options.title: Codex owns the app-server OpenAI route
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex session route owner if maintainers consider OpenAI model-agent runs primarily owned by the Codex app-server route.

options.title: Make stale auto fallback repair generic
options.body: Clear auto-sourced stale provider/model overrides whenever the configured route no longer includes the persisted override provider, without assigning canonical `openai` to a plugin owner.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an `extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts` owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and focused auto-fallback cleanup tests, leaving Codex to legacy aliases and Codex runtime ids.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged doctor/Codex route-state repair work makes this the clearest available owner-boundary decision signal.
